definition: Zeitgeist is the general spirit or prevailing outlook of a particular time. In this passage, it refers to a shared cultural influence that may shape what people in trance or altered states express.

provenance.scope: Source record fca72454f1995c69b072; pinned source text

reasons: The packet only uses “Zeitgeist” once in a speculative phrase (“a certain stratum of the Zeitgeist”) and does not support the broad dictionary gloss “general spirit or prevailing outlook of a particular time.”

The added claim that it refers here to a shared cultural influence shaping what people in trance or altered states express goes beyond the passage; the text only says James wonders whether sub-conscious selves may be susceptible to a stratum of the Zeitgeist, not that this is established or that it explains trance content.

The definition’s first claim (“general spirit or prevailing outlook of a particular time”) is not explicitly supported by the packet text; the packet uses “Zeitgeist” without giving a definition for the term.

The second sentence’s clarification (“shared cultural influence… shape what people in trance or altered states express”) is only partially supported: the packet says secondary selves get inspiration from a “stratum of the _Zeitgeist_,” but it does not explicitly frame this as a “shared cultural influence” nor connect it directly and clearly to “what people in trance… express.”
The packet does not provide enough basis to support the specific characterization of the term as “prevailing outlook” for a “particular time,” beyond its use in the spiritualist/trance discussion.
